graph_diagnosis.summary: Labor conditions, purchasing power, consumer spending, and category mix form a reusable retail-sales framework.
weaknesses: The graph has no supported interest-rate transmission path.
Several category claims and the direct retail-result links are retrospective, so category support is weak and outcome links are excluded.

search_factors.why_search: Labor and inflation conditions shape household purchasing power.
Purchasing power and outlays are the central demand transmission channel.
Economic outlook can reinforce or weaken willingness to spend.
E-commerce and durable-goods categories can make aggregate spending diverge from broad demand conditions.

checkpoints.mechanism: Stable labor and inflation conditions can preserve household purchasing power.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Labor conditions and real purchasing-power indicators agree.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Job conditions weaken or inflation erodes real income.

checkpoints.mechanism: Preserved purchasing power can enable sustained consumer spending.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Income, outlays, and consumer-demand measures are mutually reinforcing.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Households save rather than spend income gains.

checkpoints.mechanism: A stable outlook and job market can reinforce consumer spending.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Employment and broader activity indicators remain stable.

checkpoints.mechanism: Concentrated category strength need not translate into broad retail demand.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Compare category-level sales breadth with aggregate consumer spending.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Strength broadens across discretionary and nondiscretionary categories.

checkpoints.mechanism: Purchasing power, consumer demand, and the breadth of category spending combine to determine monthly retail-sales direction.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Reconcile income, outlays, employment, and category-level sales with the aggregate retail series.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Aggregate retail movement diverges from the household-demand and category evidence.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Stable purchasing power can support household demand and retail sales.
applicability_conditions: Outlays remain responsive to purchasing power.
failure_conditions: Households retrench or save income gains.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: A stable employment backdrop can support retail demand, but narrow category strength may not signal broad growth.
failure_conditions: Category gains are concentrated or employment weakens.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Category-specific strength masks softer broad household demand.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare sales breadth and category contributions with income and outlays.

forecast_audit_questions: Do labor and inflation conditions preserve household purchasing power?
Do income and outlays point to sustained consumer demand?
Is category strength broad or concentrated?
Do aggregate retail data reconcile with household-demand evidence?
